note: Hypothetical catastrophe presets for the incident briefing (backend/briefing.py). Every track is invented and generic: never a real storm's name, path or date. Tracks are [lon, lat] points; a line between two substations within radius_km of a track is knocked out (no 400-line cap). The campus, when present, is the hero data center, there to show it is not the cause.

presets.name: Gulf landfall near Fort Myers, with the data center
presets.description: A storm comes ashore from the Gulf near Fort Myers and heads northeast, while the 1,500 MW data center at Fort Myers is running.

presets.name: A Category 5 crosses all of Florida
presets.description: A hypothetical Category 5 storm comes ashore in the southwest and crosses the whole peninsula to the northeast, 60 km wide on each side of its path.

presets.name: Twenty Category 5 storms in one season
presets.description: Twenty hypothetical Category 5 storms cross the peninsula from west to east, one after another from the Keys to the north; all of their damage is counted at once.

presets.name: Heat dome + Gulf storm
presets.description: A hypothetical heat dome pushes every load to 130% of the summer peak while a storm comes ashore near Fort Myers. No data center.

presets.name: A Category 5 comes ashore on the Texas coast
presets.description: A hypothetical Category 5 storm comes ashore on the upper Texas Gulf coast and heads inland to the north, 60 km wide on each side of its path. No data center.

presets.name: A nor'easter up the Hudson Valley
presets.description: A hypothetical nor'easter tracks north from the coast up the Hudson Valley, 50 km wide on each side of its path. No data center.
